message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or agree on a different target). Points are earned by collecting cards from opponents when you finish your own hand. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1‑9, two Skip, two Reverse, two Draw Two), plus 4 Wild and 4 Wild Draw Four. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately. | | **Turn Sequence** | 1. **Draw** – If you can’t play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, keep it.
2. **Play** – Place one or more cards from your hand onto the discard pile that match either the color or the value of the top card. You may also play a Wild or Wild Draw Four at any time.
3. **End Turn** – Pass play clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). | | **Special Cards** | - **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
- **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
- **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
- **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
- **Wild Draw Four** – Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards all their cards, they win the round. They receive points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands (number cards count as face value, action cards count as 20, Wilds count as 50). | | **Scoring** | Keep a running total. First to reach the agreed point goal wins the game. | **Key Tips** - Keep track of what cards have been played to anticipate opponents’ moves. - Use Wild Draw Four strategically—if you’re forced to play it, you’ll lose points. - Remember that “Draw Two” and “Wild Draw Four” can be stacked: a player who receives a Draw Two can counter with another Draw Two (or a Wild Draw Four if allowed), forcing the next player to draw the cumulative amount. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak house rules (e.g., “draw two” stacking, “no wild draw four unless no color match”) to suit your group.
